resources.string: A qualitative view of normal voicing on an outgoing breath. Motion is slowed and not to scale.
During quiet breathing, air passes through the open glottis, the gap between the vocal folds. The gap widens as air flows in.
As voicing begins, muscles of the larynx draw the vocal folds toward the midline, narrowing the glottis.
Outgoing air sets the folds in motion
Air from the lungs pushes the closely spaced folds apart. Their elastic tissue recoils inward, and the interaction with outgoing air sustains vibration.
As the folds vibrate, the glottis repeatedly widens and narrows. The pulses in airflow generate sound waves that travel up the vocal tract.
As voicing ends, vibration dies away. The folds move apart, reopening the glottis for quiet breathing.
